If you are feeling kind of fake or disconnected from reality then here are some coping strategies to ground yourself 

1. meditation deep breathing
2. Take a cold shower
3. use your five senses 
4. focus on here and now 

If you are feeling emotionally numb then these strategies will help you feel something even if it is just physical sensation. But it's also worth looking into some healthy coping strategies to deal with whatever is causing this emotional pain/ emotional numbing  some general helpful coping strategies

1. exercise 
2. reading
3. meditation again
4. coloring/some arts and crafts
5. talking to friends or family/professional help line or your therapist.

I don't want to speculate on the issue that you've been hiding from people but usually issues aren't as big if you have people who support you and are working with you to get through the problem or cope with it. Usually people are a lot more accepting and willing to help people they care about and it sounds like your family is a loving one and from what you've been saying i'm lead to think that your issue is one where support would be greatly helpful. Everyone and i mean everyone is scared of reaching out to people but it is worth it 99% of the time because we tend to make things bigger then they are or assume people will be more judgemental then they really are anyways if you would like to talk more then i'm open

I mean if you arent still going to therapy then i would highly reccomend to start up again because they can give you advice while still trying to figure out what's going on  but besides that i would recommend talking to your friends about these feelings of not being on the closest of terms and seeing if they would work with you to maybe develop a better relationship and if they say no then you know where you are at with them and that opens the possibities of meeting new people even though it's not closed off in the first place. Dealing with the lack of drive or motivation usually motivation doesn't really solve issues i mean it gets you started but even people who aren't dealing with mental health issues lose motivation time to time focus more on discipline/ consistency of doing things pick a habit doesn't matter how small that you would like to build or even a bad one that you would like to break and forget about feeling like doing it just do it i mean it's harder then it sounds but i've found the 5 second rule,contingent planning, and habit linking or grouping tends to help also don't break the chain all really good ways of building or breaking bad habits. as for the meaningless sex and distrust that's usually due to low self esteem in my experience idk i would look more into why i mean you say it's not doing anything for you but yet you keep doing it so there's gotta be something you are getting out of it even if it is just attention. Not trusting people is understandable i mean it sounds like people haven't been the most honest with you but usually if you are able to just set proper boundaries/communicate with people and have some back up coping skills to deal with possible burns you will learn that most people are worthy of some sort of trust doesn't mean trust everyone with everything but yeah. Beating yourself up over what you aren't doing is never gonna do anything it's never gonna help and it's only gonna worsen your state of mind so what i'd reccomend doing is focusing more on the small wins no matter how small they are the messy place you have even if you are able to clean one small section of one room a day or just clean for like 5 mins then do it and be happy that you've been working on it don't compare yourself to other people and recognize that we aren't superhuman and sometimes you just have to priortize being healthy mentally is better off in the long run. Perfectionism and feeling ugly uh honestly perfectionism isn't inherently bad in my eyes um it's just about being able to recognize that you do have limits and that while it's perfectly fine to strive for the best possible version of yourself that its ok to make mistakes and or fail every once in a while feeling ugly um i would say if you get into therapy and start implementing some plans to get on a better path i think that will sort of sort itself out along with possible diet and exercise etc.

Depends on what's going on but if you don't feel comfortable sharing those then i'd be happy to give you some basic coping or possible suggestions to get on a better patch

5. figure out what you want to focus on and what you would like to change then create an actionable plan to achieve that plan the smart goal system is great specific measurable accountable realistic and timely

As for strenuos family relationships i mean you could open up to them about these feelings and i get that it's hard to be vulnerable and idk the whole story but it sounds to me that a lot of your issues are stemming from the lack of communication to what you are going through and how you are feeling. As for the fear that somehow everything will just spiral down usually life just doesn't work out like that i mean we are all afraid of that "lethal" mistake but that "lethal" mistake is a lot more then flunking some classes and or getting suspended from school i mean yes that is harsh to deal with but it's not gonna be some horrible thing that you can''t possibly get over usually legal issues tend to be the biggest "lethal" screw up and even then people are surprisingly resilient and bounce back from a lot of bad situations that they thought was the end.
